scan_report.headline: Transport capacity—not raw supply—is becoming the binding constraint across energy and trade, while manufacturing diversification is moving into operating assets.
scan_report.summary: The strongest current change is that Middle East crude exports have partly recovered while delivered energy remains expensive because tankers, insurance, refining and inventories are constrained. A second CONFIRMED formation is the financed Douala–Bangui corridor, where Cameroon has now authorised its World Bank credit within a US$1.12 billion regional program. Vietnam's new Pandora factory is an operating supply-chain diversification asset. Venezuela's oil recovery is now visibly dependent on grid rehabilitation; South Africa's private-transmission procurement remains credible but has slipped into 2027; and a claimed R100 billion Free State industrial project remains UNKNOWN until its launch produces bankable detail.
narrative: The energy shock is no longer explained by crude volumes alone. Middle East exports briefly returned to pre-war levels in late September, yet tanker rates, insurance, ship-to-ship transfers and missing refining capacity kept delivered prices elevated. Aramco says almost 3 billion barrels of gross supply have been lost since the crisis began and inventories could take up to two years to replenish. Repeated tanker incidents reported by UKMTO show why more physical supply does not immediately restore normal logistics. This energy-logistics chain is CONFIRMED.

Central Africa has a second CONFIRMED formation. The World Bank approved a US$1.12 billion multi-country program for the 1,400-kilometre Douala–Bangui corridor; Cameroon has now authorised a roughly US$391 million IBRD credit. Because the route carries more than 80% of the Central African Republic's external trade, road rehabilitation, border performance and maintenance reform have system-wide consequences rather than being a normal road project.

Vietnam's manufacturing role is broadening beyond electronics and footwear. Pandora's US$150 million Ho Chi Minh City facility has produced its first jewellery piece and is designed for up to 60 million pieces and 7,000 jobs, raising the company's global capacity by about 50% and creating its first production base outside Thailand. It is FORMING because the plant is operating but full scale and supplier localisation still have to be demonstrated.

Venezuela's oil-reconstruction ambitions expose an unusual dependency: electricity. Chevron, Eni and GE Vernova have signed energy agreements, but executives identify a grid deficit above 1,500 MW and CAF estimates roughly US$5 billion is needed to rehabilitate and automate the power system. Oil expansion therefore cannot be evaluated separately from generation, transmission and gas-to-power execution. This remains INVESTIGATE.

South Africa's first private-transmission procurement remains INVESTIGATE but carries fresh weakening evidence. Seven pre-qualified bidders completed due diligence, yet the final RFP has moved from the third quarter of 2026 to the second quarter of 2027 while guarantee and commercial structures are refined. The grid need—about 14,000 kilometres over a decade—remains, but the investable timetable has slipped.

The Free State government's announced R100 billion industrialisation project is retained as UNKNOWN. The stated manufacturing, green-economy and energy-transition scope is material, but the ceremony is still ahead and the announcement does not disclose financing, facilities, technology, land, customers or milestones. Those omissions prevent promotion.
unresolved_questions: How quickly can tanker availability, insurance and refining capacity normalise even if Hormuz crude flows recover?
Will Douala–Bangui procurement and maintenance reform translate financing into lower freight time and cost?
How rapidly will Pandora ramp Vietnam output and localise suppliers beyond direct employment?
Can Venezuela restore enough reliable power to support oil expansion without worsening household and industrial shortages?
Will South Africa issue a bankable transmission RFP in the revised 2027 window?
Does the Free State project have committed capital, defined plants and credible counterparties?

records.theme: Energy scarcity has shifted from crude supply toward logistics, refining and inventory replacement
records.location: Strait of Hormuz / Middle East / global fuel markets
records.why_surfaced: Middle East crude exports briefly recovered to pre-war levels while delivered prices stayed elevated, isolating tanker capacity, insurance, refining outages and depleted inventories as binding constraints.

world_change: Crude flows are recovering faster than the transport, refining and inventory system required to deliver usable fuels.
pressure: Repeated tanker attacks, longer routes, ship-to-ship transfers, depleted inventories and damaged refineries.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Safe tanker capacity, war-risk insurance, medium-sour refining capacity, diesel output and accessible commercial inventories.
formation: A durable energy-logistics and refining bottleneck is supporting high delivered fuel costs even when crude export volumes improve.
consequences: Persistent fuel and freight inflation
Higher working-capital and insurance costs
Pressure on fuel-import-dependent emerging markets
Demand for refinery repair, storage and tanker capacity
evidence: Aramco CEO inventory and supply-loss figures
Kpler export recovery and tanker-rate evidence reported by Reuters

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 6 October scan; it was absent from the 5 October reading layer.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Primary incident data, export-flow recovery and industry inventory/refining evidence independently converge on the same logistics mechanism.
strengthening_evidence: Aramco said on 5 October that inventory replenishment could take up to two years.
UKMTO recorded multiple tanker attacks or threats between 1 and 5 October.
Exports temporarily returned to pre-war levels without normalising delivered prices.
weakening_evidence: Higher crude export volumes have reduced the headline supply deficit from its peak.
break_conditions: Hormuz transit normalises without repeated attacks
Tanker and insurance costs return near pre-war levels
Refining capacity and inventories recover materially
new_links: Recovered crude volumes now separate the logistics/refining constraint from the upstream supply constraint.

listed_players.name: Saudi Aramco
listed_players.role: Producer with critical pipeline, storage and export infrastructure

records.valuation_research: The formation can affect upstream, tanker and refining cash flows differently. No company-level entry valuation is asserted; security research must distinguish temporary war premiums from durable capacity economics and political risk.

evidence.fact: Aramco's CEO said nearly 3 billion barrels of gross supply had been lost, more than 1 billion barrels had been drawn from stocks and replenishment could take up to two years.
UKMTO recorded repeated tanker attacks and a 5 October incident in which a tanker was instructed to turn back or be targeted.
Reuters reports Middle East exports briefly exceeded pre-war levels while tanker attacks and logistical constraints continued.
Reuters reports VLCC rates above US$1.2 million per day versus roughly US$30,000 in January and freight rising from about 3% to 27% of delivered barrel cost.

contradictions: Crude export recovery could alleviate some upstream tightness.
Industry executives have commercial incentives to emphasise scarcity and high prices.
War-risk data can change rapidly and some ship movements are obscured by disabled tracking.
missing_evidence: Country-level freight and retail fuel pass-through

records.theme: The Douala–Bangui trade corridor has moved into financed country execution
records.why_surfaced: Cameroon authorised its IBRD credit on 2 October inside a US$1.12 billion regional program for a corridor carrying more than 80% of CAR's external trade.

world_change: A 1,400-kilometre regional trade corridor is moving from multilateral approval into sovereign financing and procurement.
pressure: CAR depends on the route for most external trade while road condition, safety, borders and maintenance raise transport costs.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Road rehabilitation, border efficiency, maintenance institutions, safety and coordinated cross-country execution.
formation: A US$1.12 billion multi-phase program combines physical works with maintenance and trade-facilitation reform.
consequences: Potentially lower freight time and vehicle cost
Greater resilience for CAR imports and exports
Construction and logistics demand
Sovereign and security execution risk

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 6 October scan; absent on 5 October.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Regional approval, country credit authorisation and procurement evidence establish finance, mechanism and implementation participants.
strengthening_evidence: Cameroon's 2 October decree authorises the IBRD credit.
The wider World Bank program is approved and procurement preparation is visible.
break_conditions: Credit agreement does not become effective
Procurement or security delays prevent works
new_links: Regional program approval is now linked to sovereign credit authorisation in Cameroon.

evidence.fact: The World Bank approved a US$1.12 billion program, with a US$525 million first phase, for corridor works and reforms across Cameroon, CAR and CEMAC.
Cameroon's president authorised a credit agreement for the corridor project on 2 October.
The French decree is the original legal record authorising the IBRD credit.
evidence.source: Présidence de la République du Cameroun
evidence.english_summary: The decree authorises signature of an IBRD credit agreement for the Douala–Bangui Economic Corridor project.

evidence.fact: Reuters independently reports the authorised credit at approximately US$391 million.

contradictions: Financing and decrees do not prove lower transport costs or completed works.
The corridor crosses security- and governance-sensitive territory and requires multi-country coordination.

records.theme: Pandora has opened its first production base outside Thailand in Vietnam
records.why_surfaced: The US$150 million facility has produced its first piece and is designed to increase Pandora's global manufacturing capacity by about 50% while diversifying geography and metal inputs.

world_change: A major global jewellery brand has opened a second-country manufacturing platform in Vietnam.
pressure: Pandora seeks capacity growth, resilience beyond Thailand and reduced exposure to volatile silver through more platinum-plated products.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Skilled craftspeople, ramp quality, recycled-metal supply, supplier localisation and demand absorption.
formation: A 60-million-piece annual facility could add 50% to global crafting capacity and employ up to 7,000 people.
consequences: Vietnam gains a high-employment export manufacturing anchor
Pandora diversifies production geography
Potential local supplier and skills ecosystem

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 6 October scan; absent on 5 October.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: The facility is physically open and producing, with quantified capacity and jobs, but the full ramp and supplier ecosystem are not yet proven.
strengthening_evidence: The first piece was produced at the 1 October opening.
Company and independent sources agree on investment, capacity and jobs.
break_conditions: Quality or labour constraints prevent full scale
new_links: Geographic diversification is now embodied in an operating factory rather than a construction plan.

listed_players.name: Pandora A/S
listed_players.role: Owner and operator of the Vietnam facility

records.valuation_research: The factory adds nominal capacity equal to roughly half of Pandora's prior global base, but a security-level entry range requires demand, utilisation, margin and capital-return evidence. No recommendation is made.

evidence.fact: Pandora says its US$150 million facility will produce up to 60 million pieces annually, add about 50% to capacity and create 7,000 jobs.
Ho Chi Minh City reporting confirms the inauguration at VSIP III Industrial Park and local-government participation.
Reuters independently reports the factory is Pandora's first outside Thailand and may supply one-third of global capacity by 2030.

contradictions: Opening capacity is not the same as full utilisation.
The investment diversifies Pandora geographically but remains a single-company anchor rather than a proven cluster.
Large added capacity could pressure returns if demand underperforms.

records.theme: Venezuela's oil expansion is becoming a grid-rehabilitation market
records.why_surfaced: Large oil agreements and a GE Vernova grid alliance now collide with a power deficit above 1,500 MW and an estimated US$5 billion rehabilitation requirement.

world_change: New oil and grid agreements are attempting to restart investment in Venezuela's energy system.
pressure: Oil output expansion, households and industry compete for unreliable electricity while outages worsen.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Reliable generation, transmission automation, gas-to-power projects, equipment, finance and governance.
formation: Grid rehabilitation and self-generation are becoming prerequisite markets for oil-sector recovery.
consequences: Potential demand for turbines, substations and controls
Oil investment delayed without reliable power
Risk that energy projects crowd out household supply

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 6 October scan; absent on 5 October.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Named agreements and quantified grid deficits establish the dependency, but delivery and financing remain uncertain.
strengthening_evidence: Chevron, Eni and GE Vernova agreements were signed on 2 September.
Executives and CAF quantified the grid deficit and investment need on 30 September.
weakening_evidence: Power cuts are worsening even as investment announcements multiply.
break_conditions: Grid agreements are not funded or executed
Oil projects proceed without wider grid rehabilitation
new_links: The oil-recovery chain is now explicitly linked to grid reliability and gas-to-power investment.

records.valuation_research: Contract value, payment security, sanctions treatment and attributable earnings are not disclosed sufficiently for valuation. Exposure is contextual, not a recommendation.

evidence.fact: The US Department of Energy says Chevron, Eni and GE Vernova signed agreements covering oil expansion and grid modernisation.
Reuters reports an electricity deficit above 1,500 MW and a CAF estimate of US$5 billion to rehabilitate and automate the grid.
Spanish-language reporting says Venezuela intends to add 1,300 MW while documenting the continuing electricity crisis.
evidence.english_summary: The report describes a plan to add 1,300 MW and the scale of Venezuela's continuing power shortages.

contradictions: Government investment claims may overstate executable finance and timing.
Adding generation does not by itself repair transmission, distribution or governance.
Political and sanctions conditions can rapidly alter participation.

records.theme: South Africa's private-grid procurement is advancing due diligence but slipping into 2027
records.why_surfaced: Seven pre-qualified bidders completed investor due diligence, but the final RFP for the first private transmission program has been delayed while guarantee and commercial structures are refined.

world_change: South Africa is attempting its first private procurement of national transmission assets.
pressure: About 14,000 kilometres of grid expansion is needed over a decade while public balance-sheet and delivery capacity are constrained.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Bankable guarantees, regulatory structure, final RFP, grid connection planning and private capital.
formation: A credit-guaranteed procurement model could create a new private transmission market, but the bid window has moved into 2027.
consequences: Potential opening of a new private infrastructure asset class
Delayed renewable connections if procurement slips
Future demand for equipment and EPC capacity

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 6 October scan; absent on 5 October.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Due diligence and pre-qualified bidders show credible preparation, but the final RFP delay prevents FORMING classification.
strengthening_evidence: Seven pre-qualified bidders are engaged and due diligence took place from 28 September to 2 October.
weakening_evidence: The final RFP target moved from Q3 2026 to Q2 2027.
break_conditions: RFP slips again or is cancelled
Bid terms fail to attract finance
new_links: Investor due diligence now connects the policy concept to a defined bidder pool.

evidence.fact: South Africa says investor due diligence has occurred and a further bidder-consultation round will precede the final RFP.
The official program site says the transmission plan requires about 14,000 kilometres of lines and related infrastructure over ten years.
Engineering News reports the final RFP target has shifted to the second quarter of 2027.

contradictions: Government describes progress, while the investable RFP has slipped materially.
Transmission need does not guarantee bankable private returns or affordable tariffs.

records.theme: A claimed R100 billion Free State industrial project lacks bankable detail
records.why_surfaced: An official announcement names Chinese investors and a very large manufacturing and green-economy investment, but the launch is still ahead and the project structure is undisclosed.

pressure: The region seeks manufacturing investment, permanent employment and energy-transition activity.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Verified financing, defined facilities, land, utilities, technology, customers and delivery governance.
formation: Potential industrial and green-economy cluster if the announced capital and facilities are substantiated.
consequences: Potential 6,500 permanent jobs
Large local infrastructure demand
High announcement and execution risk
evidence: Independent reproduction of the same announcement

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 6 October scan; absent on 5 October.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: The scale is unusual enough to preserve, but evidence is not yet sufficient to explain what is being financed or built.
strengthening_evidence: A government-hosted launch and named investor are scheduled for 9 October.
weakening_evidence: The announcement provides no financing sources, facilities, timeline, technology or customers.
break_conditions: No binding finance or land agreements appear
Investor identity or capacity cannot be verified

contradictions: The claimed scale is exceptionally large relative to the detail disclosed.
The second source repeats the government advisory rather than independently verifying finance or facilities.
The launch event has not yet occurred.
